                                Original japanese recipe ^9/10/11: Hagi glaze uses twice rice straw ash than Nuka glaze.
                        Soda feldspar 1 part, rice straw ash 2 parts, wood ash 1 part.
                           Vinod Chettur recipe for ^6: use silica (for rice straw ash) + 1/2 part ulexite.
                               After doing some testing at ^5, Potash Feldspar revealed a better melt than Soda
                              Feldspar. I use wood ashes that have a lower melting temperature than "normal" ones.
                       Maybe you will need to raise ulexite percentage.
                                Attention: this glaze gelifies and never stops absorbing water. Applying it can be a                       Clara Giorello
                                                                                                                          9 years ago
                             nightmare. Adding alcohol solves the problem: 10/20% water+ 90/80% alcohol.
                          Never add Cmc to the glaze.
                        By wheight, the recipe is as it follows:

                                                                                                    Kata Pare if I remember well, I rubbed the rim with
                                                                                                      another glaze, maybe a copper/chrome one, then
                                                                                                 dipped in the Hagi.
                                                                                        The rusty "dots/strkes" come from my wood ash



                                                                                                            Anna Tartani
                                                                                                     4 months ago

                                                                                                   Hi Clara,
                                                                                             Did this glaze really melt at cone 5? According to Stull it looks
                                                                                                           that it would be severely underfired.



                                                                                                               Dan Palmer
                                                                                                           4 months ago

Anna Tartani - I said basically the same thing
                                                                                previously :) If you look above in the comments Clara
                                                                             explained that she used a specific ash from a South
                                                                     American tree to get it to melt at C5. I tried tests with
                                                                added Gerstley borate and lowered silica, and it still
                                                                                     didn't quite melt at cone 9.



                                                                                                       Clara Giorello
                                                                              4 months ago

                                                                Anna Tartani
                                                                              Yes, it has too much silica.
                                                     My ashes have a really good melt and I use ulexite.
                                                                                                                                           I didn't try this recipe again because my ulexite come
                                                                           too coarse (rocks) and it gives me too much work with
                                                                           the mortar/pestle.
                                                                                   Also, the slurry gels, and it's a nightmare to work with
                                                                                                                                   it... 🙄 adding alcohol instead of water solves the
                                                                          problem, but anyway... will try again if I find a better
                                                                          grinded ulexite.
